content.description: In October **1962**, the world spent **13 days** a hair away from nuclear war. Missiles in Cuba, fleets on alert: the Cold War reached its peak.

hero.hook: Thirteen days in which a single “yes” could have set off a nuclear apocalypse.

blocks.text: In October **1962**, humanity came within inches of the worst. For **13 days**, the United States and the USSR faced off over nuclear missiles installed in Cuba, an island less than 150 km from Florida. The bombers were ready. One mistake, and everything could tip over.

The crisis was the high point of the Cold War. It played out in offices in Washington and Moscow, and also in one isolated submarine, where an officer refused to fire a weapon that could have destroyed everything.

In **1959**, **Fidel Castro** took power in Cuba. For Washington, an ally of Moscow that close to the American mainland was unacceptable. In April **1961**, the CIA, the American secret service, staged a landing at the [[Bay of Pigs]]. It was a disaster. President **John F. Kennedy** was humiliated, and Castro moved even closer to the USSR.
To hide Operation [[Anadyr]], the secret deployment of the missiles, the Soviets also loaded farm equipment and Russian winter clothing, as if the ships were bound somewhere else entirely.

**Nikita Khrushchev**, the Soviet leader, wanted to even the balance. The Americans had already installed nuclear [[Jupiter missiles in Turkey]] and in Italy. Warheads in a NATO country like [[Turkey]], right on the Soviet doorstep, were intolerable for Moscow. So he decided to install medium-range missiles secretly on Cuban soil.

sections.title: Cuba, too close to the United States

blocks.text: On **October 14**, an American U-2 spy plane photographed launch pads for [[SS-4]] missiles, able to reach much of the United States. Kennedy gathered a small crisis committee. For six days they weighed every option: air strikes, invasion, diplomacy.

blocks.caption: The U-2 photographs reveal the Soviet missiles in Cuba

blocks.text: Generals like Curtis LeMay wanted to strike at once. Kennedy chose a middle path: a naval blockade. He called it a “quarantine” to avoid the word “blockade,” which means war in international law. On **October 22**, on television, he revealed the missiles to the world and demanded their removal.

On **October 27**, nicknamed “Black Saturday,” a U-2 was shot down over Cuba. At sea, the Soviet submarine **B-59**, harassed and cut off from Moscow, was about to launch a nuclear torpedo. The rules required three officers to agree. Two said yes. **Vasili Arkhipov**, the political officer on board, said no.
The famous “red telephone” installed after the crisis was really a **teleprinter**. The red phone only exists in the movies.

Behind the scenes, a deal took shape. The USSR withdrew its missiles from Cuba. The United States promised not to invade the island. A secret clause: the American missiles in Turkey would be pulled out later.

The crisis opened a phase of [[Détente]], a relative calm between the two blocs. A direct line soon connected the Kremlin and the White House. The doctrine of [[Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD)]] took hold: since nobody can win a nuclear war, nobody should start one.

Anadyr.explanation: Codename for the secret Soviet operation to deploy troops, aircraft, and nuclear missiles to Cuba in 1962.

April 1961.explanation: Failed invasion attempt of Cuba by Cuban exiles trained by the CIA. The humiliating failure weakened Kennedy, encouraged Khrushchev to take risks and strengthened Castro, creating the conditions for the 1962 crisis.

Bay of Pigs.explanation: Failed invasion attempt of Cuba by Cuban exiles trained by the CIA. The humiliating failure weakened Kennedy, encouraged Khrushchev to take risks and strengthened Castro, creating the conditions for the 1962 crisis.

Bay of Pigs Invasion (April 1961).explanation: Failed invasion attempt of Cuba by Cuban exiles trained by the CIA. The humiliating failure weakened Kennedy, encouraged Khrushchev to take risks and strengthened Castro, creating the conditions for the 1962 crisis.

Détente.explanation: Period of the Cold War (1962-1979) characterized by a desire for dialogue, peaceful coexistence and nuclear arms limitation treaties.

Jupiter missiles in Turkey.explanation: American nuclear missiles installed in Turkey in 1961, within reach of the USSR. The final secret agreement included their discreet withdrawal - a concession that Kennedy kept secret for decades so as not to appear to be yielding to Soviet blackmail.

MAD.explanation: Nuclear doctrine stating that neither the United States nor the USSR could survive a nuclear war. This logic of balanced terror deterred everyone from attacking and structures the entire dynamic of the Cuban crisis.

Mutually Assured Destruction.explanation: Nuclear doctrine stating that neither the United States nor the USSR could survive a nuclear war. This logic of balanced terror deterred everyone from attacking and structures the entire dynamic of the Cuban crisis.

Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD).explanation: Nuclear doctrine stating that neither the United States nor the USSR could survive a nuclear war. This logic of balanced terror deterred everyone from attacking and structures the entire dynamic of the Cuban crisis.

SS-4.explanation: Soviet intermediate-range ballistic missiles deployed in Cuba, capable of reaching most of the American territory.

The Bay of Pigs Invasion.explanation: Failed invasion attempt of Cuba by Cuban exiles trained by the CIA. The humiliating failure weakened Kennedy, encouraged Khrushchev to take risks and strengthened Castro, creating the conditions for the 1962 crisis.

The Bay of Pigs Invasion (April 1961).explanation: Failed invasion attempt of Cuba by Cuban exiles trained by the CIA. The humiliating failure weakened Kennedy, encouraged Khrushchev to take risks and strengthened Castro, creating the conditions for the 1962 crisis.

Turkey.explanation: NATO member country where the United States had installed Jupiter missiles, constituting one of the reasons for the Soviet response in Cuba.

To obtain a permanent naval base in the Caribbean
